notes: `כָּל־יְמֵי` is marked `noncompositional` because *for as long as* spends nothing on either morpheme in particular; the source head is `יְמֵי`, the one morpheme whose lexeme is written among the English words (*long*), so rule 6's first-token fallback does not reach it. `כֹּל` is the competing anchor.
*threescore and ten* is kept whole with `שִׁבְעִים`; no waw stands between two Hebrew numerals there (rule 42).
`שָׁבָתָה` → *it kept sabbath* is headed on the complement under rule 44, *kept* alone naming nothing of the lexeme.
